title: The Growth Kinetic and Ultra High Hardness of CoCrFeNiTi High–Entropy Alloy by Mechanical Alloying and Spark Plasma Sintering

recollection.starting_material: Guess: Equiatomic elemental powders of Co, Cr, Fe, Ni and Ti
recollection.intervention: Guess: High-energy mechanical alloying (ball milling) followed by consolidation via spark plasma sintering
recollection.structure: Guess: Ultrafine-grained single-phase FCC matrix containing a nanoscale dispersion of Ti-rich BCC/Laves intermetallic precipitates
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Severe plastic deformation and repeated cold welding during milling produce a supersaturated solid solution; rapid SPS heating locks in ultrafine grains and precipitates that impede dislocation motion
recollection.results: Guess: Fully dense (>99% theoretical) bulk alloy with Vickers hardness around 1000–1200 HV (≈9.8–11.8 GPa)

score.note: The intervention merely restates the title without milling time, atmosphere, or SPS conditions. The proposed FCC matrix with Ti-rich BCC/Laves precipitates conflicts with the reported 83% FCC/17% BCC nanocrystalline phase mixture. The mechanism partially captures milling-induced deformation, supersaturated solid solution formation, and grain refinement retention, but incorrectly emphasizes precipitate strengthening and omits the reported Hall–Petch/dislocation synergy. The estimated 1000–1200 HV and >99% density are unsupported and far from the reported 675 HV; strength values were omitted.
